NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A plan to drain the marsh would destroy the birds' home: gather and sing against it, or offer another plan.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Some villagers want to drain the marsh to make new gardens. (subject) says the marsh is where half the island's birds nest. (friend) says the village needs more land. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) and many others gather at the marsh's edge, singing the birds' song and telling stories of the marsh. The plan is put aside. The village is still short of land, and (friend) is still looking for some.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) finds an old overgrown field on the hill that could be cleared instead. It is harder work than draining the marsh. The village agrees, grumbling. The birds never know how close it was.
